clue.text: Thus little boy creates disgust

parts.note: sic is Latin for 'thus', used to mark a quotation as printed
Ken is a boy's name, short (little) for Kenneth

explanation.surface: A small child's behaviour is causing revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: To sicken someone is to make them feel nauseated or repelled.

clue.text: High charge increased, among a variety of extras

indicators.note: among places one piece inside the other
a variety suggests a mix, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: something increased has gone up

explanation.surface: An expensive fee rises with assorted add-ons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' is not 'raised' here: the definition is the whole phrase 'High charge', a levy on high earners, while 'increased' gives the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An additional tax on high incomes is a steep levy.

clue.text: A romance developed around Northern Irish region

indicators.note: around places the rearranged letters round the next piece
developed means grown into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A love affair blossoms in the north of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges A ROMANCE, and 'around' wraps it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: This area of County Galway in the west is a district of Ireland.

clue.text: Origins of Europe mentioned in this broadcast

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so take the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: European roots are referred to in this programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast something is to send it out, as a signal is sent.

clue.text: Terrapin's not a terribly fast mover

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not tells us the word a is left out of the letters before it

parts.note: the possessive is read as its letters, terrapin plus S

explanation.surface: A turtle is hardly a speedy creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes one A from TERRAPINS, leaving TERRPINS, and 'terribly' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is a runner over short distances, built for speed.

clue.text: School place is secured, it's assumed

indicators.note: secured means held fast, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
a site is a place

explanation.surface: A pupil's place at a school is taken for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is a group of whales, a POD, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something posited is put forward as a premise, supposed true.

clue.text: Snooker player may be wanted by the police?

definitions.text: Snooker player may be wanted by the police?

parts.words: Snooker player may be wanted by the police?
parts.note: a snooker player at the table is playing a frame; a suspect is also said to be under suspicion in this phrase

explanation.surface: A snooker star is a police suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: A FRAME is one game of snooker, and a suspect the police want is said to be in the frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means under suspicion, and literally playing a game of snooker.

clue.text: Take top off solid piece of furniture

indicators.note: taking the top off a down entry removes its first letter

parts.note: something stable is solid and steady

explanation.surface: Remove the top from a sturdy piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-topped item with legs for eating or working is household furniture.

clue.text: Gives response concerning elements of play

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a play is divided into acts

explanation.surface: Someone answers about parts of a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something.

clue.text: Respectable characters in trade centre

indicators.note: characters in means some of the letters inside the words

explanation.surface: Decent people are found at a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Being proper and of good standing is respectable.

clue.text: Poor writer takes river boat

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the Nile is the great river of Egypt
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An impoverished author embarks on an Egyptian river cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no money at all is poor in the extreme.

clue.text: I closed my teeth around a bone

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the phrase before it round, reading it backwards

parts.note: closing your teeth on something means you bit it, so I BIT

explanation.surface: Someone recalls biting down on a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses I BIT to TIBI, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone of the lower leg is a long bone.

clue.text: Regretted have governed without centre left

indicators.note: without centre says the middle letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to govern is to rule

explanation.surface: A former ruler laments having been in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of RULED happens to be L, the abbreviation for 'left', so that is what goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to feel sorry about it.

clue.text: Colony's agreement

explanation.surface: A settlers' outpost signs a treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a community of settlers founded somewhere new, and a deal resolving a dispute is likewise a formal accord.

clue.text: Hoot, catching a boy dressing

indicators.note: catching means holding something within

parts.note: a hoot is a scream, something very funny
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A screamingly funny scene where a boy is getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoot' means something hilarious, not an owl's call. SALAD CREAM is a British bottled condiment rather like mayonnaise.
explanation.definitionFit: This tangy sauce is a dressing poured on a salad.

clue.text: Firm churned out data about worker

indicators.note: about places the first letters around the second piece
churned suggests the word is stirred about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a man is a worker, as in a man employed on a job

explanation.surface: A company has mass-produced figures concerning an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun beside 'worker', but it is the adjective meaning resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unshakeable in their resolve is firm and immovable.

clue.text: Frank's aim

explanation.surface: A man named Frank states his goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain-speaking candour is the first sense; to point something at a target is the second.

clue.text: On watch in disorderly part of San Francisco, perhaps

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Keeping watch in an unruly district of a Californian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese quarter is a neighbourhood found in San Francisco and many other cities.

clue.text: Inexperienced players not finishing drink

parts.note: green means new and inexperienced

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: Novice players fail to finish their drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' cuts the final M from TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfermented tea leaves make a popular hot drink.

clue.text: Old man's given chopped vegetable and fruit

parts.note: papa is an informal word for father, an old man

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a yam is a starchy tuber eaten as a vegetable

explanation.surface: Dad is served some cut-up vegetables and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' cuts the final M from YAM, leaving YA.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical tree bears large orange-fleshed melons, a fruit.

clue.text: Leave a group of people working

parts.note: a band is a group of people
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Departing a team of people at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon something is to leave it behind.

clue.text: With bounder about, one's more nervous

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: something that bounds is a leaper or jumper
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone with a cad around grows more anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' seems to be the old word for a cad, but here it is one who bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Being jittery or easily startled is a sign of nerves.

clue.text: Famous singer's car (German)

parts.note: a Jag is a Jaguar car

explanation.surface: A celebrity singer drives a German car.
explanation.walkthrough: Mick JAGGER fronts the Rolling Stones.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rolling Stones' frontman, Mick, is a celebrated rock singer.

clue.text: Artist raised objections over total rubbish

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts
BS is short for bull, complete nonsense

explanation.surface: A painter protested about complete nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns BUTS upwards into STUB. George STUBBS was an English painter famous for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: George, the eighteenth-century horse painter, was an artist.

clue.text: Accept person in care is to rule the roost

parts.note: to accept something is to take it
a charge is someone placed in another's care, like a ward

explanation.surface: Admitting a dependant means becoming the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling the roost is being in command, assuming control.

clue.text: Executioner's vessel

explanation.surface: The hangman owns a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack, the notorious 17th-century English hangman, gave his name to executioners; a two-masted sailing boat is the vessel.

clue.text: Mist in Middlesex location, we've heard

indicators.note: we've heard signals that the letters sound like the word before

parts.note: Hayes is a town in Middlesex, a former county west of London

explanation.surface: Fog descends on a town in the London suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: MIDDLESEX is a historic English county now mostly absorbed into Greater London.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin fog or vapour blurring the air is a mist.

clue.text: Wine that, in test, is tastiest

indicators.note: in says the wine's letters sit inside the word test to make the later word

parts.note: the wine's letters sit inside this word only because the clue builds it by putting them in test: a coincidence of the construction, not a hidden-word device

explanation.surface: This wine, when tried, is the most delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the wine's letters in TEST (T-ASTI-EST) and you get TASTIEST; so take TEST's letters out of TASTIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: This sparkling white from Piedmont is an Italian wine.

clue.text: Go swimming with male at club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man takes a dip at his sports club.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to take a swim in the sea or a pool.

clue.text: Fashion code, with stars in formal wear

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A dress code for celebrities requires formal clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like the first half of DRESS CODE but is a verb: rearrange CODE and STARS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailcoat worn for evening occasions is formal clothing.

clue.text: School fellow entertained by a French or German musician

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: un is French for a
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A student is hosted by a composer from France or Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a French' gives UN, the French for 'a'; 'or' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert, the Romantic composer, was a German musician.

clue.text: After struggle, Napoleon gutted a European capital

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: After a battle, a defeated emperor flees to a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' empties NAPOLEON, keeping only its first and last letters, N and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian capital on the Danube is a European capital city.
